title: Work, Energy and Simple Machines
summary: Grade 9: work done by a force, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, power and electricity units, and how levers, pulleys and ramps help us.

ib.statementOfInquiry: Energy is never created or destroyed, only transferred and transformed; understanding this helps us design machines and use energy more sustainably.

factual: When is work done by a force?
How are kinetic and potential energy calculated?
conceptual: Why can a machine reduce the force needed but not the work done?
Where does the 'lost' energy go when a ball stops bouncing?
debatable: Should homes be charged more per unit when they use a lot of electricity?
Is it better to design machines for speed or for efficiency?
